findings.problem: The appendix heading renders as h2#appendix-scriptural-date-and-location, while the site's responsive dossier rules recognize only sec:date-location and scriptural-date-and-location. Consequently these tables receive the generic horizontally scrolling table layout instead of the required stacked narrow layout. In the actual full-document browser DOM at a measured 500-pixel viewport, six dossier tables exceed their 437-pixel visible width (Entrance 473 pixels; Corinthians 523 pixels), and the faithful focused-section screenshot visibly clips the Entrance Composition label and date behind a scrollbar. This violates the web-edition rule that every dossier column remain visible at narrow widths; the existing heading test misses the Appendix-prefixed form.
findings.required_result: Make the generated appendix participate in the site's existing dossier presentation while preserving its heading, all eight dossiers and their explanations. Repair the publication conversion/rendering contract rather than hand-editing the generated Markdown, cover the Appendix-prefixed heading in the owning check, regenerate the canonical web edition, and verify that every chronology column is visible without horizontal table scrolling at narrow widths while desktop remains readable.
